subject: Maths
title: Rationalising the denominator
subtitle: Surds · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can rationalise the denominator of a fraction containing surds.

key_vocab.definition: Rationalising means removing the surd from the denominator. Multiply top and bottom by the surd in the denominator (or its conjugate).

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can rationalise the denominator of a fraction containing surds.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Rationalising -- Rationalising means removing the surd from the denominator. Multiply top and bottom by the surd in the denominator (or its conjugate).

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the surd (or conjugate) to make the denominator rational.
&frac{a}{√b} = &frac{a × √b}{b}
Since √b × √b = b

Key examples:
  ✓ &frac{1}{√3} = &frac{√3}{3}  (multiply top and bottom by √3)
  ✓ &frac{4}{√2} = &frac{4√2}{2} = 2√2  (then simplify)
  ✓ &frac{1}{1+√2} × &frac{1-√2}{1-√2}  (use the conjugate)
  ✗ &frac{1}{√3} = &frac{1}{3}  (must multiply both top and bottom)
  ✗ &frac{3}{√5} = &frac{3}{5}  (denominator becomes 5, but numerator becomes 3√5)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – simple rationalisation
  Rationalise &frac{1}{√5}.
  Multiply top and bottom by √5
  &frac{1 × √5}{√5 × √5} = &frac{√5}{5}
  Denominator is now rational
  &frac{√5}{5}
  (Multiply by √5 over √5 (which equals 1).)

Example 2 – with a coefficient
  Rationalise &frac{6}{√3}.
  Multiply top and bottom by √3
  &frac{6√3}{3}
  Simplify: = 2√3
  2√3
  (After rationalising, simplify the fraction.)

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ To rationalise &frac{1}{√3}, multiply top and bottom by √3
✗ &frac{1}{√5} = &frac{1}{5}
✓ The conjugate of 3 + √2 is 3 - √2
✗ &frac{4}{√2} = 4√2
✓ (a + √b)(a - √b) = a² - b
